text: Before data lands in the star schema from Lesson 8, something has to decide which source column becomes which target column — tedious, repetitive work an LLM can draft quickly.
Give an LLM the source columns, target columns, and sample rows, and it proposes a mapping with a confidence signal per pair.
A wrong test case fails loudly and gets caught. A wrong schema mapping ships silently — every downstream report is now quietly wrong.
Never load a mapping straight from the proposal — check every low-confidence pair against real sample data, and spot-check the high-confidence ones too.
Confidence signals help triage, but only real sample data confirms a mapping. Next up: guardrails on what not to hand an LLM.
